title: Design Neighbor Sum Service
summary: Design a class that stores a square n x n grid (n from 3 to 10) whose cells hold distinct integers in [0, n*n - 1]. Because there are exactly n*n cells and n*n distinct values in that range, every value appears exactly once, so every lookup target exists. The class needs two query methods: adjacentSum(value) returns the sum of the values directly above, below, left and right of the cell holding value (only cells inside the grid count); diagonalSum(value) returns the sum of the values in the four diagonal cells of that position (again only cells inside the grid count). Each query is answered from the stored grid.
inputFormat: Constructor: NeighborSum(grid) with grid an n x n integer matrix. Method calls: adjacentSum(value) and diagonalSum(value) with value an integer in [0, n*n - 1].
outputFormat: Constructor returns nothing (null in the call trace). adjacentSum and diagonalSum each return one integer: the sum of the qualifying neighbour values. For n >= 3 every cell has at least one adjacent neighbour and at least one diagonal neighbour inside the grid, so the sum is over a non-empty set of cells.
officialConstraints: value passed to adjacentSum and diagonalSum is in [0, n*n - 1]
At most 2 * n*n calls in total to adjacentSum and diagonalSum
constraintsReportedBySource: Recovered raw statement lists the constraints above; not yet confirmed on the official page in this pass.
tieRules: Not applicable: each query returns a single sum; no ties.
edgeRules: Neighbour cells outside the grid contribute nothing (corner and edge cells have fewer than four adjacent or diagonal neighbours).
The queried cell itself is never included in its own sum.
Because values are distinct and cover [0, n*n - 1], the queried value is always present in the grid; no 'value not found' behaviour is specified.
